description:
Run virtual services in your network

You use VirtServer to run virtual services in your network. It is an addition to ReadyAPI Virtualization that is used for creating, editing, and running virtualized services.
VirtServer is tightly integrated with ReadyAPI Virtualization, allowing you to run and manage virtual services created with ReadyAPI Virtualization and hosted on VirtServer. VirtServer runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, and headless machines .
Features and improvements
- ReadyAPI version 4.3.0 compatibility: Updated for compatibility with ReadyAPI 4.3.0. For version pairings, see ReadyAPI and VirtServer Compatibility Matrix.
Bug fixes
- Fixed an issue where memory use increased with each redeployment of a virtual service. VirtServer now releases the project that it opens temporarily during redeployment, so memory use stays stable, and pods no longer restart for this reason.
- Fixed an issue where the Windows installer placed a new VirtServer version in the folder of a previously installed version. The installer now creates a separate folder for each version.
- Fixed an issue that prevented VirtServer from starting on Linux when you installed it system-wide as an administrator. VirtServer now checks /etc/virt-server/ for the keystore and truststore files if they are not located in ~/.readyapi/virt-server/. Files in ~/.readyapi/virt-server/ take precedence.
